subject: maths-aa-sl
author: original (NevaIB)
title: Arithmetic sequences and series

points.text: General term of a sequence with constant difference
Sum of the first n terms; sigma notation
Modelling with arithmetic patterns, including data that is only approximately arithmetic

bigPicture: An arithmetic sequence adds the same amount each step. Two formulas (term and sum) answer almost every question; the hard part is setting up n correctly.

keyIdeas.cue: General term of an arithmetic sequence?
keyIdeas.answer: u_n = u₁ + (n − 1)d, where d is the constant difference between consecutive terms.

keyIdeas.cue: Sum of the first n terms; how do you read sigma notation?
keyIdeas.answer: S_n = n/2 (2u₁ + (n − 1)d) = n/2 (u₁ + u_n). Σ from k = a to b adds the expression for each integer k; it has b − a + 1 terms.

keyIdeas.cue: When is an arithmetic model appropriate?
keyIdeas.answer: When a quantity changes by a constant amount each step (rows of seats, fixed weekly savings). If data are only roughly arithmetic, use the average difference and treat predictions as approximate.

keyTerms.def: d = u_(n+1) − u_n, the same for every pair
the sum of the terms of a sequence

misconceptions.right: The first term already counts once: u_n = u₁ + (n − 1)d.

misconceptions.wrong: Σ from k = 3 to 10 has 7 terms

practice.prompt: An arithmetic sequence has u₄ = 17 and u₁₀ = 41. Find d, u₁ and S₂₀.
commonErrors: Using 7d or 5d between u₄ and u₁₀

practice.prompt: A theatre has 24 seats in the first row and each row has 3 more seats than the row in front. (a) How many seats are in row 30? (b) What is the least number of rows needed for at least 1000 seats?
commonErrors: Using u_n instead of S_n in (b)

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

given.item: u_n = u₁ + (n − 1)d; S_n = n/2 (2u₁ + (n − 1)d) = n/2 (u₁ + u_n)
